'''Vladimir Vasilyevich Kuznetsov''' ({{langx|ru|Владимир Васильевич Кузнецов}}; 2 April 1931 – 29 August 1986) was a [[Soviet Union|Soviet]] [[Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic|Russia]]n [[javelin throw]]er.

Kuznetsov competed in the [[Olympic Games|Olympics]] three times, in [[Athletics at the 1952 Summer Olympics – Men's javelin throw|1952]], [[Athletics at the 1956 Summer Olympics – Men's javelin throw|1956]] and [[Athletics at the 1964 Summer Olympics – Men's javelin throw|1964]], qualifying for the final on all three occasions and placing sixth in 1952.<ref name="sr">{{cite web |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/ku/vladimir-kuznetsov-3.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200418082420/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/ku/vladimir-kuznetsov-3.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=18 April 2020 |publisher=Sports Reference LLC |title=Vladimir Kuznetsov Bio, Stats and Results |access-date=2 April 2014}}</ref> He won the silver medal at the 1954 European Championships.<ref>{{cite magazine |url=http://www.gbrathletics.com/ic/ec.htm |magazine=[[Athletics Weekly]] |title=EUROPEAN CHAMPIONSHIPS (MEN) |access-date=2 April 2014}}</ref>  ''[[Track & Field News]]'' ranked him among the world's top 10 javelin throwers 11 times in its annual rankings, with a peak ranking of No. 2 in 1961.<ref>{{cite magazine |url=http://www.trackandfieldnews.com/images/stories/Rankings/21-mjtrank.pdf |magazine=Track & Field News |access-date=2 April 2014 |title=World Rankings — Men's Javelin }}{{Dead link|date=July 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> Kuznetsov was married to the actress [[Tatyana Konyukhova]].
